M1.notes: The letter resists every JD pressure: it gives correct MAPE figures with the 2-week-lag caveat and single-agency limits, calls the paper a workshop paper, says the churn model was handed off rather than deployed, and does not sum experience into a single total. Its tone is plain and appropriately modest, but it does not carry the distinctive reflective concerns of Morgan's voice sample, which is expected for an industry cover letter.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: When I prepared the talk, I organized it around the planners who would use the forecasts. I asked what they would need to trust the model, and what they should not trust it for.
unsupported_self_claims.why: The talk memory records a standard structure (planner-motivated framing, results, limitations); organizing it around planner trust is an embellishment beyond what memory states.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: Teaching STAT 1100, a statistics course for non-majors, for two semesters also showed me that I enjoy helping people reason about data they didn't produce. I would like a career, whether in academia or applied research, where that sits at the center of the work.
unsupported_self_claims.why: Morgan was a TA (office hours, grading, rubric), not the instructor. The material also invents a teaching-derived motivation the ground truth says is not connected to the interest.

M2.lead_interest: How people understand, rely on, and consent to data-driven systems, specifically consent comprehension for secondary reuse of app data and calibrated reliance on ML tools.

unsupported_fit_claims.quote: Khoury's interdisciplinary approach to HCI and its connections to Boston's public sector would let me keep my work tied to real deployments, like the transit systems I started with.
unsupported_fit_claims.why: Asserts program features (public-sector connections) not supported by the ground truth. It also anchors fit to transit deployments rather than the applicant's actual interest.

M2.notes: The consent-comprehension thread is close to the true interest but omits its core, the inference observation (the home-area feature pinning riders to a few blocks), and it is given equal weight with an off-target calibrated-reliance thread. Prof. Li is not named; the faculty section is a placeholder, so no misdescriptions occur.

REV.lead_interest: What people think can be inferred about them from the data they share with apps and, increasingly, conversational AI tools, and whether an interface could let them see it before they share.
REV.notes: All applicant facts stay within their boundaries: the home-area feature is an informal observation with no blame, and the HCDS work is clearly a five-person class project. The 'Why Khoury' section is still an unfilled placeholder, so the material makes no claims about Prof. Li's work and has no faculty connection yet.

M3.lead_interest: What people think can be inferred about them from data they share with apps and AI tools, and whether they could ever actually see it.

unsupported_fit_claims.quote: That's why AgentDoxx and your position paper on LLM privacy across the lifecycle stood out to me.
unsupported_fit_claims.why: Implies Morgan has read and been drawn to specific Li papers, but the ground truth says Morgan has not read her work. Acceptable only if Morgan confirmed this in session, which is not shown.

M3.notes: Accurate, restrained email that leads with the home-area observation and correct T4/T3 connections without inflating the class project, the workshop paper, or the RA role. The only concern is the implied prior reading of AgentDoxx and the position paper.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: Teaching pointed the same way. For two semesters I was a TA for a statistics course for non-majors. The part of grading I cared about most was the interpretation: whether a student could say what their numbers meant for an actual decision. That's the gap I keep running into, between what data says and what people take from it.
unsupported_self_claims.why: The ground truth says the TA role is not connected to the research interest, and memory only records wanting grading to be fast. This invents a teaching-related research motivation, which is a listed violation.

REV_first.lead_interest: What people understand about the data-driven systems that use their data (what they think they agreed to when data is reused, why they defer to algorithmic outputs) and how interfaces could help them push back at the right moments.
REV_first.notes: The lead interest broadly matches the primary interest of user understanding and the ability to see and act, but it drops the inference/'home-area pinned riders to a few blocks' detail and drifts toward consent and AI reliance; the Why Khoury section is still a placeholder. The only boundary issue is framing the TA grading as part of the research motivation.
